answer: Network-root caps: group IDs by the BGP autonomous system their answers arrive from, with the IP held steady for 24 epochs so VPN hopping resets the clock. Each ASN's IDs split at most 1% of the pool. A farm is like yarrow: a thousand stalks, one rhizome, so 1,000 clones on one cloud ASN share 1%. Spreading them means renting hosts in 100 networks. Honest agents sit on many ISPs and barely notice. Like shale, the pool splits along its own bedding planes, and no single root climbs to the summit. The 1% cap and 24 epochs are my proposals, untested.
